# secret scan — accepted findings, by blob fingerprint
######################################################
#
# THE FILENAME IS DELIBERATE AND WAS FORCED BY THIS GATE FINDING IT. The obvious
# name, `secret-scan-accepted.txt`, is reported by the project scanner's
# FILENAME layer — `(^|[._\-])secrets?([._\-]|$)`, "a filename naming a secret"
# — so the table was a finding of its own the first time the gate ran over a
# clone containing it. The only fingerprint that could suppress that is keyed on
# this file's own blob oid, which changes every time an entry is added, so the
# suppression would have gone stale on every edit. `.gitleaksignore`'s header
# records the same shape arrived at through CONTENT (its first draft quoted the
# line it suppressed and produced a finding about itself); this one came through
# the NAME. The name it has now is the more accurate one in any case: this file
# holds fingerprints, and it holds no secret.
#
# ONE ENTRY PER FINDING, BY BLOB FINGERPRINT. A fingerprint is
# `<blob-oid>:<engine>:<detector>:<locator>` and it suppresses exactly one match
# by one detector at one offset of one blob. Nothing else.
#
# THE KEY IS THE BLOB OID, WHICH IS BETTER THAN `.gitleaksignore`'S COMMIT KEY
# AND WORSE IN ONE STATED WAY. Better: a blob oid is the sha1 of the CONTENT, so
# an entry survives a rebase, a filter-branch and a rename, and it can never
# suppress DIFFERENT content — a changed byte is a different oid and the entry
# stops matching. `.gitleaksignore`'s own header records the opposite cost for
# its `commit:path:rule:line` form. Worse: an oid says nothing about WHICH
# commit introduced the blob, so every entry below names that separately, in
# prose, from `git log --find-object`.
#
# DESCRIBE, NEVER REPRODUCE. `.gitleaksignore` learned this the expensive way:
# its first draft quoted the line it was suppressing, which put the same string
# into the suppression file and produced a second finding — at
# `.gitleaksignore:28`, which is now an accepted finding of its own, twice over
# (once for gitleaks, and the historical blob is in this file's table below).
# A suppression file that quotes what it suppresses will suppress itself into
# existence.
#
# DELIBERATELY NOT AVAILABLE, and each for the same reason — every one of them
# would suppress findings nobody has looked at, including ones that do not exist
# yet:
#
#   * no path pattern. A path is not content; the same path holds a new blob
#     tomorrow.
#   * no detector-level or rule-level disable. `credential_assignment` is the
#     detector most likely to catch a provider this project has never heard of,
#     and `generic-api-key` is gitleaks' equivalent.
#   * no oid-level wildcard. A blob accepted for one detector at one offset is
#     not accepted for a second detector that starts firing on it.
#
# ADDING AN ENTRY IS NOT A FIX. Two of the three blocks below are FALSE
# POSITIVES and one is a REAL CREDENTIAL that is still in this repository's
# history and is not removed by being written down here. Read the block.
#
# To re-derive this list after a deliberate history change:
#     python .github/scripts/secret_scan_gate.py --emit-accepted
# It PRINTS; it never writes this file. Every line still has to be looked at and
# given a reason, which is the whole point.


# ===========================================================================
# BLOCK 1 — A REAL CREDENTIAL, STILL IN HISTORY. NOT A FALSE POSITIVE.
# ===========================================================================
#
# Twelve historical blobs of `docker-compose.yml`, each carrying a hardcoded
# value for the Airflow web signing key under a variable spelled
# `AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__SECRET_KEY`. Two syntactic shapes across the twelve: the
# older environment-LIST form (`- NAME=<value>`, two blobs, 56-character value)
# and the later mapping form (`NAME: <value>`, ten blobs, the capture one longer
# because it takes the leading space). The value itself is described and not
# quoted, per the rule above: fifty-six characters of letters, underscores and
# hyphens with NO DIGIT ANYWHERE, ending in words that ask the reader to change
# it in production.
#
# HOW IT SURVIVED A SCANNER FOR SO LONG, and it is the reason this project's own
# detector has a length cap. `_is_program_identifier` in
# oncotriage/staging/secrets_scan.py exempts a captured value that looks like a
# NAME — letters, underscores, hyphens, no digit — because fifteen of the first
# seventeen findings this scanner ever produced were exactly that. Unbounded,
# that exemption matched this value exactly, and `scan_bytes` over the real
# compose file returned ZERO findings: a hardcoded signing key in a file the
# scanner called clean. `_IDENTIFIER_EXEMPTION_MAX_LENGTH = 48` is what made it
# visible, and this value at 56 is the measurement that set the ceiling.
#
# gitleaks reports NONE of these twelve, on any of its ~170 rules, in either
# `git` or `dir` mode. A digitless letters-and-punctuation string clears no
# entropy floor it has. That asymmetry is why this gate runs two engines.
#
# WHAT WAS DONE, AND WHAT WAS NOT. HEAD no longer carries it: the compose file
# sources both Airflow secrets from the environment (`${...:?}`), so the working
# tree is clean. The literal remains in every commit that carried it and is
# therefore in every clone. It is treated as COMPROMISED and must never be
# reused — which is the honest state, because a signing key that has been in a
# repository about to be made public is spent whatever anybody writes here.
#
# WHY IT IS ACCEPTED RATHER THAN REMOVED. Removing it means rewriting pushed
# history: every SHA below it changes, every `.gitleaksignore` fingerprint keyed
# on a commit stops matching, and several tests in this suite derive a revision
# and lift negative controls out of `git show`. That is a decision with its own
# blast radius and its own review, and it is not made by a scanner.
#
# REMOVAL CONDITION: these twelve entries go when history is rewritten, and the
# gate FAILS WITH EXIT 2 if they are left behind afterwards — a stale accepted
# entry is re-read by the next person as a live constraint.
#
# Introduced across the compose file's life; `git log --find-object=<oid>` names
# the commit for any one of them.
002f75e72280051454310d1d7e32d55a54a5aa71:oncotriage:credential_assignment:16591
238480f723636b9132e0803c4ab4bde4edb10039:oncotriage:credential_assignment:11868

# ===========================================================================
# BLOCK 2 — A SYNTHETIC SENTINEL IN A TEST. NOT A CREDENTIAL.
# ===========================================================================
#
# Three historical blobs of `tests/test_tracking_mlflow_index.py`, each
# assigning a module-level constant whose name says what it is — a SENTINEL —
# to a 32-character string beginning `sk-`. That test seeds a fake API key into
# the environment and then requires the MLflow parameter enumeration to carry it
# in no key and no value; the string has to LOOK like a key or the assertion is
# vacuous, which is this project's standing rule about degenerate checks.
#
# It matches this project's `openai_anthropic_key` detector, which asks only for
# `sk-` followed by twenty or more identifier characters. It matches NO gitleaks
# rule: gitleaks' `openai-api-key` requires the literal infix `T3BlbkFJ` and one
# of two exact lengths, neither of which a fabricated sentinel has.
#
# It is usable against no service. `python s3_stage.py` has refused on it since
# before this gate existed, which is where it was first written down.
#
# REMOVAL CONDITION: these three go when history is rewritten, or when the
# sentinel is changed to a shape no detector matches — for which the honest
# instrument is the staging exclusion manifest rather than a shape chosen to
# slip past a scanner.
30b65d019735cb0002941f876b51e28f5b4b00e3:oncotriage:openai_anthropic_key:18436
5698d07120cc8eb1ff473b60019697d23c5844ec:oncotriage:openai_anthropic_key:21703
e5932da50468c43e944c296ab71b468a91e2d193:oncotriage:openai_anthropic_key:18436

# ===========================================================================
# BLOCK 3 — A QUERY REGISTRY KEY. NOT A CREDENTIAL. ALREADY ARGUED IN
#           `.gitleaksignore`, HERE UNDER THE OTHER FINGERPRINT FORM.
# ===========================================================================
#
# Six blobs: five historical versions of `oncotriage/storage/queries.py` and one
# historical version of `.gitleaksignore` itself. In each, gitleaks'
# `generic-api-key` rule fires on the first keyword argument of a `Query(...)`
# record — an argument literally named `key`, whose value is the report's
# identifier: a long lower-case snake_case metric name made of English words
# joined by underscores, ~31 characters, which clears the rule's entropy
# threshold on length alone. The same construction appears ~40 times in that
# file; these are the versions where one of them crossed the threshold.
#
# THE SIXTH IS `.gitleaksignore`'S OWN FIRST DRAFT, and it is the reason the
# "describe, never reproduce" rule at the top of this file is written down
# twice. That draft quoted the offending line in order to explain it, which put
# the same string into the suppression file and produced a second finding at
# line 28 of it. The comment was rewritten to describe rather than quote; the
# old blob is still reachable, so the historical copy is still matched.
#
# `.gitleaksignore` ALREADY CARRIES BOTH OF THESE, keyed `commit:path:rule:line`
# — which is the form `gitleaks git` emits and the form that stops matching
# after a rebase. This gate scans blobs, so it sees the same two causes under
# five and one blob oids respectively, and it needs its own entries. The two
# files are not redundant: `.gitleaksignore` governs the commit-attribution
# scan in the workflow, this table governs the object scan.
#
# Nothing at any of these lines is secret, rotatable, or usable against any
# service. The whole file is read-only report SQL.
#
# REMOVAL CONDITION: these six go when history is rewritten, or if the query
# registry's key naming ever changes such that no key clears the entropy floor.
3bf20365b992ede199abbcc5453d38f405e7c96f:gitleaks:generic-api-key:505
